findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Resolve the marklas-vs-adf.py-extension fork so a single end-state has fully-applicable ACs (e.g. make the corpus check a gating spike that decides the path BEFORE the build ACs, or add parallel ACs covering the adf.py-extension fallback's vendored-sha-N/A and fixed-point requirements).
evidence: 'Default to a VENDORED copy under src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/ ... if it fails, we fall back to extending adf.py's handlers in-house'
AC1: 'marklas is vendored under src/rebar/_vendor/marklas/ with the upstream sha recorded'
AC6: 'MD→ADF→MD is a fixed point for ≥99.6% ... a miss triggers the adf.py-extension fallback'
findings.finding: The Approach permits a fork — vendor marklas (default) OR fall back to extending adf.py's handlers in-house if the corpus check fails — but every Acceptance Criterion is written for the marklas-vendored end state (first AC requires the vendored sha; corpus AC is framed as 'verifies marklas'). If the fallback fires, those ACs become moot/contradictory and no AC covers the correctness of the hand-rolled fallback implementation.
findings.location: Approach step 2 vs Acceptance Criteria (bullets 1 and 6)
scenarios: marklas misses the 99.6% corpus bar and the executor takes the adf.py-extension branch, leaving the vendored-sha AC unsatisfiable and the fixed-point AC unverified for the branch actually shipped
findings.suggested_fix: Reframe the corpus idempotence as a decision spike whose outcome selects the implementation, then state the build ACs against the selected path; or explicitly add fallback-branch ACs (no vendored sha; adf.py-extension passes the ≥99.6% fixed point).

findings.checklist_item: Specify that the conversion-failure fallback keeps `to_wire`, `decode_inbound`, and `normalize_outbound` mutually coherent (all three degrade to the plain-text path for that body) so the pinned law `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` still holds on the fallback path.

findings.location: Approach step 4 (Failure path); AC 'A conversion failure falls back to the plain-text ADF encode'
scenarios: A body whose markdown_to_adf raises falls back to text_to_adf for to_wire, but normalize_outbound still computes adf_to_markdown(markdown_to_adf(t)); decode_inbound(to_wire(t)) then decodes the plain-text ADF differently -> comment/description diff never converges for that body

findings.checklist_item: Reason through and cover the comment-diff path: with `normalize_outbound` now markdown-aware but `normalize_rich_text` kept plain-text, show the two comment-diff keys still converge (or scope AdfCodec's markdown normalize to descriptions only), else the DIG-5301 duplicate-comment asymmetry returns for markdown comment bodies.

findings.finding: Making `AdfCodec.normalize_outbound` Markdown-aware while the scope guard keeps `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text` plain-text creates a comment-diff key asymmetry: the local-side key (`codec.normalize_outbound`) becomes markdown-aware but the Jira-side key (`_normalize_comment_body` -> `normalize_rich_text`) stays plain text, so markdown comment bodies stop converging.
findings.location: Scope guard ('normalize_rich_text ... stays plain-text') vs Approach step 1 (repoint normalize_outbound)
scenarios: A comment body containing `**bold**` or a heading: local key = adf_to_markdown(markdown_to_adf(body)) (markdown-preserving); Jira key = adf_to_text(<ADF Jira stored>) (plain text) -> keys differ -> the differ re-emits the same comment every pass
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep AdfCodec.normalize_outbound's comment usage plain-text-compatible, or update the comment differ's Jira-side key to decode via the markdown-aware path for Cloud, and add a comment-body convergence test with markdown formatting.
